29.0.0.en: Then Jacob lifted up his feet: he hastened on his way.

29.0.1.en: The land of the people of the east: the region of the Tigris and the Euphrates, which lies east of Canaan.

29.0.2.en: After Jacob was reassured, since God had appeared to him on the ladder, his spirit revived and he hastened on his way toward Mesopotamia, where his uncle Laban lived.

29.1.0.en: Jacob reached a field near the city of Haran, the city of Laban, which lies between the two rivers, and he found a well and three flocks of sheep waiting there with their shepherds, and on the well was a great stone covering it. They used to put it there to keep the water of the well from dust, and because it was large a group of shepherds would gather to roll away the stone and then water the flocks. When Jacob reached the shepherds, he asked them about Laban and how he was, and they said, We know him, and he is well. He asked them the reason for their waiting, and they said, Until all the flocks are gathered, so that it will be easy for us to roll the stone away. Then they told him that Rachel, Laban's daughter, was coming from afar with the sheep that she kept.

29.2.0.en: When Jacob finished speaking with the shepherds, Rachel had reached the well with the sheep of her father Laban, and Jacob rejoiced greatly at seeing her, so much so that he went up to the well and rolled away the heavy stone, alone or with the help of the waiting shepherds, and went forward and watered the flock of his uncle Laban. As for Rachel, she was looking with wonder at this man who cared for her and her sheep.

29.2.1.en: Jacob is a type of Christ, Rachel of the Church, and the well of Baptism, while the waiting flocks are a type of the world awaiting Christ the Savior. For Christ rolled away the stone, that is, the barrier of sin between Himself and mankind, and renewed His Church through Baptism, which became an image of the redeemed before the whole world, to draw them toward salvation.

29.3.0.en: Her father's brother: a nephew, whether sister's or brother's son, was sometimes called a brother.

29.3.1.en: My bone and my flesh: my relative, so you have the right of hospitality.

29.3.2.en: Jacob told Rachel that he was the son of her father's sister Rebekah and kissed her with joy, and she was delighted and ran to her home to tell her father of the arrival of Jacob from the land of Canaan.

29.4.0.en: When Laban heard of the arrival of the son of his sister Rebekah, he hastened to him, kissed him, and welcomed him into his house. Jacob told Laban all the events of their life in Canaan, their works and their possessions, and how he had a brother named Esau, and how he had taken the birthright and the blessing from him, so that Esau bore a grudge against him, which forced him to flee to Haran. His uncle reassured him and rejoiced in hosting him for a month, during which he helped his uncle in tending the sheep and all the work required.

29.4.1.en: As long as God is with you, He guides you in all your steps and gives you grace in the eyes of all, and even gives you strength to carry out His will, so be reassured and trust in Him and enjoy His presence with you.

29.5.0.en: Jacob was working diligently to help his uncle without wages, for mere food that he ate, and after a month had passed and Jacob had settled in tending the sheep, Laban asked him what wages he wanted to take from him.

29.6.0.en: Jacob loved Rachel, the younger daughter of Laban, and wanted to marry her, and since he had no possessions or money to give as a dowry to her father, he proposed to his uncle that he would serve him for free for seven years, and his wages during this period would be given as a dowry to marry Rachel. Laban accepted, declaring that it was better to give her to him because he was his relative and surer than strangers, especially as he had lived with him for a month and knew his character.

29.7.0.en: Jacob worked tending the sheep of his uncle Laban for seven years with all care and diligence, and did not complain of the length of the period or the amount of effort he exerted, but felt that it was the least he could offer as a dowry for Rachel whom he loved.

29.7.1.en: If you love God, you will accept toil for His sake in many prayers and fasts, and even service for His holy name, and you will see that the toil is sweet because it is a response to the divine love poured out on the Cross, so you will strive to please God whatever the cost and sacrifice, and press upon all your circumstances to be with Him.

29.8.s.en: (3) Jacob's marriage to Leah and Rachel

29.8.0.en: Laban's exploitation of Jacob appears here. After waiting a month, he used Jacob in his service under the name of hospitality and then fixed his wages; now seven years pass, and we do not know whether the one who fixed them was Jacob or his uncle Laban. It is of course a long period and its wages great, since marriages did not then require expenses other than a tent and simple furniture. But in any case, at the end of the seven years Laban did not give his daughter to Jacob until he demanded it of him, so he was trying to exploit him as much as he could.

29.8.1.en: Take care not to exploit others, however weak they are or difficult their circumstances, and however great your authority, because God the Almighty sees you and is grieved by your greed. On the contrary, the more generous you are, the more God honors you, and the more you exploit, the more God deprives you of His blessings.

29.9.0.en: Laban made a wedding feast and invited his neighbors to rejoice with him at the marriage of his daughter to Jacob, and when night fell Laban gave his daughter Leah to Jacob and gave her a maidservant named Zilpah. So Jacob went in with his bride to the tent that Laban had prepared for them. The bride covered her face with a red veil, and because of the similarity of the voice and the darkness inside the tent, Jacob did not know who was with him and thought she was Rachel.

29.10.0.en: In the morning, in the light of day, Jacob discovered that the one he had married was Leah and not Rachel, and he was very distressed and hastened to reproach Laban for deceiving him. He excused himself by saying that it was not proper, according to the custom of the place where they lived, for the younger to marry before the elder, so he had been compelled to give him Leah. He then made a proposal, exploiting Jacob's love for Rachel and showing Laban's material greed, offering Jacob to complete a week of feasting with Leah as was the custom of that time, and then give him Rachel, on condition that he serve him another seven years for free as a dowry for the second wife.

29.10.1.en: Thus, as Jacob deceived his father and took the blessing, so also Laban deceived him, that God might make him taste the bitterness of deceit so that he would turn away from it.

29.10.2.en: When God permits you tribulations or wrongs from others, do not complain, but examine yourself to know your sins, which deserve far more than these tribulations, and in proportion to your submission to God's will and your acceptance of the tribulation, God will reveal to you many benefits of the tribulation.

29.11.0.en: After the week of marriage with Leah was completed, Jacob married Rachel, and her father also gave her a maidservant named Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah and served another seven years to complete the dowry, that is, he served 14 years for free to marry Rachel his beloved.

29.12.0.en: Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, which caused Leah distress, and this is one of the problems of polygamy, which disappeared in Christianity, and perhaps her distress was increased because she had agreed with her father in deceiving him. In any case, God felt her suffering and compensated her with children, while God withheld Rachel from bearing, since she was barren, lest she be proud against her sister.

29.12.1.en: Leah is a type of the Jewish people, to whom God gave many offspring, and from them came Levi, that is, the tribe of the priesthood, and also Judah, from whom Christ was born. As for Rachel, she is a type of the Gentiles, who were unable to bear spiritual children to God because of their distance from the faith, but Christ, of whom Jacob is a type, offered salvation to both, the Jews and the Gentiles, and afterward the Gentiles became fruitful in Christ after they believed.

29.12.2.en: Wonderful is God in His arrangements for the salvation of your soul: He supports you in tribulation and honors you so that you are not swallowed up by grief, and at the same time permits you tribulations if you are prone to pride or to dominating others, because He seeks the salvation of your soul by every means, so submit to Him and accept His will, for it is always for your good.

29.13.0.en: When Leah bore her firstborn son she rejoiced, since this would make Jacob love her, and she named him "Reuben," which means, behold, a son.

29.14.0.en: God gave Leah a second son because of her prayers before Him, and she called his name "Simeon," which means heard, because God heard her prayers to bear sons.

29.15.0.en: God gave Leah a third son and she rejoiced in him and called him "Levi," which means joined, because she said, With the birth of three sons Jacob will be joined to me and will not be distant from me.

29.16.0.en: God also blessed Leah with the birth of a fourth son, and she called him "Judah," which means praise, because she thanked God for the abundance of His gifts. Then she stopped bearing for a time, lest she too be proud against her sister.

29.16.1.en: How beautiful it is that you name your children with names that have spiritual meanings beneficial to them and to you, because a person's name is dear to him and he holds fast to it, so it is an opportunity that brings him near to God by its beautiful meaning.

30.0.0.en: Rachel suffered because of her barrenness, and instead of taking refuge in God by prayer, she complained against her husband and demanded that he give her sons, and felt that her life without sons was like death and had no purpose. This shows the extent of her despair, because she had heard from Jacob of God's blessing on his offspring and saw that Leah with her children would obtain the whole blessing. Sadly, Rachel's absorption in the material inheritance appears here, and she did not perceive the spiritual inheritance and the importance of her attachment to Jacob in order to learn true faith from him.

30.0.1.en: May you accept God's arrangements for your life, because they lead to the salvation of your soul, and in proportion to your being spiritual you will understand God's purposes. Care for all that brings you near to God, because it remains forever, and do not be carried along with the current of the world, preoccupied with passing material things.

30.1.0.en: Jacob was angry at Rachel's complaining and directed her heart to prayer, because God alone is the giver of sons.

30.2.0.en: She shall bear upon my knees: that is, she will bear and give me sons whom I will carry on my knees.

30.2.1.en: Rachel did not benefit from the mistakes of her grandmother Sarah and repeated the same deed, asking her husband to lie with her maidservant, and the sons would be counted as Rachel's, as was the custom of that time. It would have been better for her to pray and wait for God to give to her if He willed, and if not, to thank Him and accept her condition and not depend on her human thoughts.

30.3.0.en: When Jacob lay with Bilhah she conceived and bore a son, and Rachel called him Dan, because she felt that God had judged for her and vindicated her, for Dan means judgment.

30.4.0.en: Bilhah bore a second son to Rachel and she called him Naphtali, that is, my wrestling, because she felt her wrestling and rivalry with her sister over bearing sons, for after her sister had borne four sons she was able to bear two through her maidservant. It is a bad thing that Rachel felt this struggle with her sister instead of love and friendliness, whereas the fruit, namely sons, is given by God.

30.5.0.en: Leah was influenced by the mistake of her sister Rachel and fell like her into the same mistake, giving her maidservant Zilpah to Jacob so that she might bear sons for her, because she had stopped bearing for some time. She bore her a son whom she called Gad, which means fortune, because she said that God had given to me with fortune, that is, made me happy by the birth of this son.

30.6.0.en: Then Zilpah bore a second son to Leah and she called him Asher, which means blessed, because she said that God had made me happy.

30.6.1.en: Do not rush to imitate those around you, for they may be mistaken even if they are the majority of those around you, but ask God first, and the Church, and they will guide you.

30.7.0.en: Mandrakes: the fruit of trees resembling the apple or the plum, which the common people call the jinn's apple, and they believe that it draws the husband to love his wife, and this is of course a belief with no basis of truth.

30.7.1.en: Reuben, the son of Leah, went out to the field and found a mandrake plant, and brought some of its fruit to his mother, who rejoiced in it, believing, like the people of her time, that it draws the husband to love his wife. But Rachel saw the mandrakes with Leah and asked her to give her some of them.

30.8.0.en: Leah was troubled by Rachel's request, because the struggle between them was great and the feelings of love between them had weakened, and because Jacob loved Rachel and was attached to her and neglected being with Leah after she had stopped bearing. So she said angrily to Rachel, Is it a small matter that you have taken my husband, and would you take my son's mandrakes also, so that Jacob may be more attached to you? Rachel said to Leah, Give me some of these mandrakes, and I will make Jacob lie with you tonight.

30.8.1.en: Do not let your relationship with those around you be material and utilitarian, but let your relationship with God be the basis of your relationship with them, confident that God blesses you from heaven as long as you trust in Him. Do not be troubled by the gains of others so as to be jealous of them and envy them, but ask God to give to you, and your soul will be calm and satisfied with His love and overflow with love to those around you.

30.9.0.en: Leah went out to meet Jacob when he returned from his work and told him what had happened with her sister and how she had taken the mandrakes in exchange for his coming to her. Jacob agreed and went in to lie with her, and Leah lifted up her prayers to God, and she conceived after having ceased bearing for a long time, and bore a son whom she called Issachar, which means he works for wages, because she said that God had given me my wages when I agreed to give my maidservant Zilpah to him. This is a hard thing for any wife, that her husband should lie with her maidservant, but she accepted this so that she might have more sons, so God granted her to bear again, and she bore Issachar.

30.10.0.en: Leah conceived again and bore a sixth son and called him Zebulun, that is, dwelling, because she said, Because I have borne six sons, now my husband will care for me and dwell with me, since he was bound more to Rachel and spent most of his time with her.

30.11.0.en: The Scripture mentions a daughter whom Leah bore and called Dinah, and the meaning of her name is judgment, being the feminine of the name Dan. Probably other daughters were born to Jacob, but it mentions Dinah because of an event in which Dinah will appear, namely her relationship with Shechem (ch. 34).

30.12.0.en: At the end of the fourteen years Rachel bore Joseph, and thus the difference in age between him and his firstborn brother Reuben was 13 years. Rachel's state of mind improved after she bore, and likewise Leah had become settled in mind after bearing six sons, so the struggle between them calmed. Jacob felt that he had worked 14 years for free for Laban, giving his labor during them as a dowry for his two daughters, so he asked to depart from him in order to begin work that would give him wages sufficient for his children and more, to provide for the needs of his large family, made up of two wives and two concubines and 11 sons, apart from the daughters. Jacob was longing to return to the land of Canaan, whose inheritance God had promised to him and his fathers.

30.12.1.en: Do not be preoccupied with the world and material things away from your goal, which is to be with God in the Church, where your true place is, but arrange your life so that its foundation is your relationship with God, and spend the rest in the works of the world and the needs of the body, so that your enjoyment of God may be continuous.

30.13.0.en: Jacob showed Laban how much he had toiled in tending his sheep and asked him to permit him to depart with his wives and children.

30.14.0.en: Laban said to Jacob, If I have found favor in your eyes, stay with me, because you have been a cause of blessing to me and my possessions have increased, and take whatever wages you see fit.

30.15.0.en: The Lord has blessed me for your sake: God gave you blessing because of me.

30.15.1.en: Jacob declared to Laban the extent of his toil in tending his sheep and how God had blessed him because of his service to him, so that the small flock that was with Rachel became very many flocks during the fourteen years. And he repeated to Laban that he needed to work and save for his large family.

30.16.0.en: Speckled: black in color with a few white spots.

30.16.1.en: Spotted: white in color with many black spots.

30.16.2.en: Jacob did not ask for a monetary reward for his work but asked to take some of the sheep, and specified them as the sheep whose color differed from the prevailing color among the sheep, which is white tending toward yellow. Some sheep are black or have black and white spots or have white stripes, and these strange colors, which are found rarely among the sheep, Jacob asked to be separated out and given to him.

30.17.0.en: Laban agreed to Jacob's request because it was a small wage, since the sheep of different color were few among the flocks, and he separated these sheep and gave them to his sons, who were the sons of Jacob, meaning his grandsons, or gave them to his sons to give them to Jacob. Because Laban's sheep were very many, he set a distance between his sheep and Jacob's sheep of a three days' journey, that is, about 40 miles. And Jacob continued to tend Laban's sheep in addition to his own sheep.

30.18.1.en: Storax: a plant from which, if its outer bark is removed, a milk-white liquid flows, called balsam resin, and it is used in incense.

30.18.2.en: Hazel: the well-known plant that gives the fruit of the almond.

30.18.3.en: Chestnut: a plant found in the plains and on the banks of rivers.

30.18.5.en: Troughs: the basins of water from which the sheep drink.

30.18.6.en: Many people in ancient times, and some even until now, believed in prenatal impression, which is that if a pregnant female, human or animal, sees something, the newborn comes out in the same form. This is of course a mistaken thought that Jacob believed, so he used rods from which he peeled parts so that they would be like his striped and spotted sheep, but God blessed this mistaken belief of his because he was wronged by his exploiting uncle Laban, so He blessed his flocks and they increased, as appears from the dream he saw in (ch. 31:12). Perhaps Jacob used a scientific method of breeding to increase his possessions: he brought green plant rods and peeled rings and spots on them so that they became spotted and striped, and from some of them even a milky liquid flowed, so the rods appeared mottled, resembling his mottled and striped sheep. He placed these rods in the places where the sheep drink at the mating season, so that when the white sheep look at these rods they become familiar with them and like them because they drink water beside them, which is essential for their life, and after they drink he puts before them his mottled and black sheep, so the white sheep mate with the mottled, and bear mottled sheep, that is, spotted and speckled. Thus the sheep belonging to Jacob increase, and Jacob separates them from among Laban's sheep and takes them for himself.

30.19.0.en: Jacob did another thing in breeding the sheep for his benefit, which is that at the mating season, if he found Laban's strong white sheep coming to drink, he placed the peeled rods at the water so they became familiar with them, and brought to them his mottled sheep so they mated with them. And if he found Laban's white sheep of the weak kind, he removed the peeled rods and let them mate with the rest of his white sheep. Thus the mottled sheep belonging to Jacob became strong and the white sheep belonging to Laban became weak.

30.20.0.en: By this Jacob's possessions increased and multiplied, and he bought many male and female servants. Jacob's return to Canaan
